premise — both lookups really ran
why: 🔴 THE PLACEMENT IS THE PROPERTY. Without this check the resolver claims the order, stamps the attempt captured (manual_verified) and commits `confirmed` before anything asks whether this caller can refund — so every state change the decision was meant to prevent has already happened by the time anyone asks. The cell seeds the attempt UNSTAMPED and asserts manual_verified is absent afterwards, which is the direct observable; the two-lookups cell's premise also stops holding, because only one lookup runs. 🔴 THIS NOTE PREVIOUSLY SAID the order would be left confirmed because the guard's park could not accept `confirmed`. That was true when it was written and is FALSE at HEAD: Q-1 widened the park to accept a confirmed order precisely so the two-hours-lookup race could not strand one. The mutant still dies, but on premature stamping rather than on stranding — a stale rationale on a live mutant is how the next reader mis-scopes a fix, so it is rewritten rather than left to be reinterpreted.

why: 🔴 RESTORED AFTER I DELETED IT AS UNREACHABLE, WHICH WAS WRONG. There are TWO hours lookups: the early one before the claim, and the guard's own, after the attempt is stamped captured and the order committed `confirmed`. If the early lookup throws or the kitchen's hours change between them, only the guard sees closed — and with the park refusing a confirmed order it answered 'held' anyway: HTTP 200, no park, no alert, captured money, unmaterialized, eligible for automatic recovery. `confirmed` is not an in-flight reversal; it is the state this path just created.
